items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Paul Meers, one of the greatest classical dancers that New York ever knew

ctx.x: being engaged to replace Don Redman in Connie's Inn. Ed Kirkenby wrote in his book about 'Fats' Waller, (Ain't Misbehavin), that Don Redman was the last orchestra to play Connie's Inn, but Russell was the last band to play there. Connie still owes me and the rest of Russel's men $200.00 in back pay.

The show was great in Connie's with Louise Cook who was a beautiful shake (1) skane-dancer, Paul Meers, one of the greatest classical dancers that New York ever knew and his second wife, 'Jazz Lips' Richardson, a comic acrobat dancer, the one and only 'Snake Hips' Tucker, The Lucky Seven Trio, three fellows who danced on big blocks made to represent dice, three girls who had a singing act, and 12 beautiful chorus girls.

But Connie's was beginning to lose the white clients from downtown because Harlem was turning bad and so many white people were getting robbed when they came uptown. And negros, the few that ever went to the place, were treated so bad they got the tables where it was almost impossible to see the floor show, so they did not come there when the place started losing the white customers. This happened in 1933. I had rejoined Russell in 1932.
